annotations.text:
Four directions, all on the same light/dark token set.
Every artboard has a Theme tweak above it — flip it to see the dark values.
Light is the default everywhere, as asked.

Nothing here is implemented yet.

A — REFINED CONSOLE
Today's layout, cleaned up. Status band merged into one row, delivery tiles given a real hierarchy, fleet compressed to one strip.

Why: lowest risk, ships fastest, nothing to relearn.
Tradeoff: still scrolls — evidence and hypothesis sit below the fold on a laptop.

B — SIDEBAR WORKBENCH
Persistent left rail holds tenant, pool, scenario controls and the theme switch. Main area splits fleet (left) from investigation (right).

Why: nothing below the fold; the rail is where run history and audit would live as the app grows.
Tradeoff: most structural change, and the investigation column is narrow for long evidence.

C — INVESTIGATION TIMELINE
The run is the page: a vertical spine of steps, each carrying the actual figures it read, ending in the approval gate. Fleet reduced to a KPI strip up top.

Why: this is the story judges came for — it shows the agent reasoning, not just its output.
Tradeoff: weakest for at-a-glance monitoring; poor as an idle screen.

D — DENSE OPS GRID
Everything on one screen, no scrolling, monospace-forward, hairline borders. Reads like a real operations console.

Why: highest credibility as a production tool; most information per pixel.
Tradeoff: 9-10px type is unreadable on a projector, and it is intimidating cold.
Light derived from the existing dark palette rather than invented beside it — same hues, accents darkened to hold contrast on white. Dark values are unchanged from tailwind.config.js.
